item.text: The existing app already covers project and task creation, so I’ve kept those flows and added persisted archive state plus list summaries and filters. I’m checking the changes now, including behavior against a fresh SQLite database.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc 'node --check server.js && node --check public/app.js && git diff --check && git diff --stat'
/bin/bash -lc 'node --check server.js && node --check public/app.js && git diff --check && git diff --stat'

/bin/bash -lc 'set -e
DB_PATH=/tmp/workboard-check.sqlite PORT=18765 npm start >/tmp/workboard-check.log 2>&1 &
server_pid=$!
trap '"'kill \""'$server_pid" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -f /tmp/workboard-check.sqlite /tmp/workboard-check.sqlite-shm /tmp/workboard-check.sqlite-wal'"' EXIT
for i in "'$(seq 1 30); do curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:18765/health >/dev/null && break; sleep 0.2; done
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:18765/health
project=$(curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18765/api/projects -H '"'content-type: application/json' -d '{\"name\":\" Demo \"}')
printf '%s' \""'$project"
project_id=$(node -e '"'let s=\"\";process.stdin.on(\"data\",d=>s+=d).on(\"end\",()=>process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(s).id))' <<<\""'$project")
curl -fsS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:18765/api/projects/$project_id/tasks" -H '"'content-type: application/json' -d '{\"title\":\"Check\"}'
curl -fsS -X PATCH \"http://127.0.0.1:18765/api/projects/"'$project_id/tasks/$(curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:18765/api/projects/$project_id/tasks" | node -e '"'let s=\"\";process.stdin.on(\"data\",d=>s+=d).on(\"end\",()=>process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(s)[0].id))')\" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{\"completed\":true}'
curl -fsS \"http://127.0.0.1:18765/api/projects?filter=Active\"
curl -fsS -X PATCH \"http://127.0.0.1:18765/api/projects/"'$project_id/archive" -H '"'content-type: application/json' -d '{\"archived\":true}'
curl -fsS \"http://127.0.0.1:18765/api/projects?filter=Archived'
"
